gloss: whether one likes it or not; willy-nilly

definitions.gloss: whether one likes it or not; willy-nilly; without choice
definitions.explanation: Describes a situation where something happens regardless of one's wishes or consent. The person affected has no say in the matter.

examples.japanese: {否応|いやおう}なしに{参加|さんか}させられた。
examples.english: I was made to participate whether I liked it or not.

examples.japanese: {時代|じだい}の{流|なが}れは{否応|いやおう}なしに{人|ひと}を{変|か}える。
examples.english: The flow of the times changes people whether they like it or not.

examples.japanese: グローバル{化|か}は{否応|いやおう}なしに{進|すす}んでいく。

notes:
A literary and somewhat formal expression. Composed of {否|いや} (no, unwilling) and {応|おう} (yes, willing), it literally means "without yes or no" — that is, without being given the choice. Most commonly used with に as an adverb: {否応|いやおう}なしに.

FORMS:
- {否応|いやおう}なく: same meaning, slightly more common in modern usage
- {否応|いやおう}なしに: the most standard adverbial form

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {否応|いやおう}なしに{巻|ま}き{込|こ}まれる: to get dragged in regardless
- {否応|いやおう}なしに{変|か}わる: to change whether one likes it or not
- {否応|いやおう}なしに{従|したが}う: to comply without choice

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {有無|うむ}を{言|い}わさず: without letting someone object — stronger, more forceful
- {強制的|きょうせいてき}に: compulsorily — more formal and administrative
- しょうがなく: reluctantly — focuses on the person's resignation rather than the external force
